notes: Cap share measures what a team PAID, not how the five played. It underrates any line built on rookie contracts -- five good young starters on rookie deals price out near the bottom of the league, and that is a real error in the rating, not noise.

The five starters are read off snaps the season actually produced, which is hindsight. At a draft you have a projected line, and the projection is wrong often enough (injury, camp battle, a guard kicked out to tackle) that the live version of this rating is weaker than the one measured here.

Contracts come from Over The Cap via nfl_data_py at run time and are joined on gsis_id; linemen with no gsis_id on their contract row are simply unpriced, which is most of what the coverage number is measuring.
overturns: The project's first pass tested the O-line rating against running back fantasy points, found nothing, and concluded the line does not matter. It measured the wrong outcome: the effect is on yards per carry, and fantasy points bury it under volume and touchdowns.
question: Does offensive line quality affect player production -- and if it does, which measurement of production shows it?
title: The offensive line pays in yards, not points
